forms.name: Small Claims Case Information Sheet / Petition
forms.description: Primary small claims filing form for Texas Justice Courts. Each precinct may have its own version.

forms.name: Civil Case Information Sheet
forms.description: Required cover sheet for civil filings in Texas.

steps.instruction: Determine the correct precinct. File in the Justice Court precinct where the rental property is located or where the defendant resides.
Complete the small claims petition form (available from the Justice Court clerk or via eFileTexas.gov).
File in person at the Justice Court or e-file at eFileTexas.gov.
steps.note: E-filing is mandatory in Harris County for represented parties. Self-represented litigants may e-file or file in person.

steps.instruction: Serve the defendant. In Texas Justice Courts, the court will typically arrange service through a constable or process server upon payment of the service fee.
steps.note: Service by constable is the most common method.

steps.instruction: Attend the hearing on the scheduled date with all documents and evidence organized.

service_of_process.method: Constable, process server, or certified mail with return receipt

filing_instructions.hearing_info: Hearing typically scheduled 21-45 days after service is completed. Both parties present their case to the Justice of the Peace.

filing_fee.condition: Small claims up to $20,000 (base filing fee; may vary slightly by precinct)

fees.fee_waiver_form: Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs (Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 145)

statute_of_limitations.statute_ref: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code §16.004 (breach of written contract)
statute_of_limitations.description: 4 years for breach of written contract; 2 years for oral contract.
